issues.body:
JSON-LD 1.1 API §5.3.2 step 1 (`@type: @id`) and step 2 (`@type: @vocab`) both say: "return a new map containing a single entry where the key is @id and the value is the result of IRI expanding value". The map is returned unconditionally; IRI Expansion (§5.2 step 2) may yield null, so the spec-literal result is `{"@id": null}`. Reference processors agree (jsonld.js `_expandValue` returns `{'@id': _expandIri(...)}`, and its `_expandIri` returns null for a keyword-shaped non-keyword).

The diff replaces this with `let id = active_context.expand_iri(s, true, false)?;` (src/expand.rs:890, :894), so the whole value is dropped, and `expand_element` step 4.3 (src/expand.rs:180) now propagates `None` — which step 13.9 (src/expand.rs:350) turns into `continue`, dropping the property.

Two evidence problems:
- The comment being deleted carried a concrete W3C citation (expand/0122-out retains `"@id": null`, manifest noting the result "will not be valid JSON-LD"). The replacement offers no spec citation — only "rather than manufacturing an empty node reference for callers to retain", which is a caller-convenience argument, not a normative one.
- The pinned W3C suite is not present in this checkout (`tests/w3c/json-ld-api` does not exist), so the `expand` conformance lane SKIPs and cannot corroborate the flip.

Internal inconsistency, verified at PR head: the `@id`-KEYWORD path at src/expand.rs:461-464 is untouched and still does `None => set_obj(result, "@id", json_null())`, explicitly citing expand/0122. Probe results:
  {"@context":{"@vocab":"http://ex/"},"@id":"@kw","p":"v"} -> [{"@id": null, "http://ex/p": [{"@value":"v"}]}]
  {"@context":{"@vocab":"http://ex/","p":{"@type":"@id"}},"p":"@kw"} -> []
Both arise from the identical IRI-Expansion-returns-null condition; the spec handles them identically (store the result). One path keeps null, the other now drops.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) revert to the spec-literal `{"@id": json_null()}` and keep `expand_value -> Json`, or (b) if the drop is genuinely intended, justify it with a normative citation or a named W3C expand test that the retaining behaviour fails, apply it consistently to the `@id`-keyword path at src/expand.rs:461-464, and record the conformance delta. Do not land a flip of citation-backed behaviour while the conformance lane is SKIPping; run the expand lane with the suite fetched (scripts/fetch-jsonld-tests.sh) and report the before/after pass counts in the PR body.
issues.title: expand_value returning Option diverges from §5.3.2 steps 1-2, which return the {"@id": ...} map unconditionally

issues.body:
Expansion step 13.8.3.7 is unconditional once container includes `@index`, index key is not `@index`, and expanded index is not `@none`:
  13.8.3.7.3 index property values = [re-expanded index] ++ existing values of expanded index key in item
  13.8.3.7.4 add (expanded index key -> index property values) to item
  13.8.3.7.5 if item is a value object it MUST NOT contain extra properties -> invalid value object, abort

The diff wraps 13.8.3.7.3-5 in `if let Some(reexpanded) = reexpanded` (src/expand.rs:818-825), so when re-expansion is null nothing is added and the MUST-abort of 13.8.3.7.5 never fires. The new test then asserts that the input expands successfully to `[{"http://ex/items": [{"@value": "kept"}]}]`, enshrining the suppression.

Verified at PR head:
  items: {"@kw":  "kept"} on `kind` (@type:@vocab) -> OK  => [{"http://ex/items": [{"@value":"kept"}]}]
  items: {"real": "kept"} on `kind` (@type:@vocab) -> ERR => InvalidValueObject

So the same shape of document — a property-based index over a value object — now aborts or silently succeeds purely on whether the index token happens to be keyword-shaped. The existing W3C expand/pi05 case (cited at src/expand.rs:820-821) still errors only because its index is not keyword-shaped, so the regression is invisible to the suite.

The reasoning that "nothing was added, so item gained no extra property, so no error" is circular: it holds only under this PR's own premise that Value Expansion returns nothing, which §5.3.2 does not say.
issues.fix_hint: Keep 13.8.3.7.3-5 unconditional. If Value Expansion is to keep returning `Option`, still add the entry (with `json_null()` as the re-expanded index, per §5.3.2) so 13.8.3.7.5 can fire, or evaluate the value-object check independently of whether the prepend happened. Then change this test to `assert_expand_error(..., JsonLdErrorCode::InvalidValueObject)` (the helper already used at tests/expand.rs:431/557/607), and add the non-keyword sibling as a paired case so the two cannot silently diverge again.
issues.title: New test property_index_null_re_expansion_is_dropped pins away the spec-mandated invalid value object abort (step 13.8.3.7.5)

issues.body:
Returning `None` from step 4.3 interacts with the two enclosing paths differently:
- Scalar: `expand_element` returns `None`, step 13.9 (src/expand.rs:350) drops the property, the node object is empty, so the whole node is dropped.
- Array: the step 5.2.3 loop (src/expand.rs:139-143) drops the `None` item and returns `Some(Json::Arr(vec![]))`, which is NOT `None`, so step 13.14's `add_value_as_array` (src/expand.rs:389 — whose own comment notes asArray is always true so an empty expansion still materialises the property) emits the property with an empty array.

Verified at PR head with `{"@context": {"p": {"@id": "http://ex/p", "@type": "@id"}}, ...}`:
  "p": "@kw"    -> []
  "p": ["@kw"]  -> [{"http://ex/p": []}]
  "p": ["@kw", "http://ex/ok"] -> [{"http://ex/p": [{"@id": "http://ex/ok"}]}]

Before this change both the scalar and single-element-array forms produced the identical `[{"http://ex/p": [{"@id": null}]}]`, so the asymmetry is introduced here. Semantically equivalent inputs (JSON-LD treats a scalar and a one-element array the same at this position) must not expand to different documents, and `{"http://ex/p": []}` is a property materialised from a value that was dropped — distinct from the normatively-retained empty arrays of expand/0004/0014/0015/0016, which are empty in the INPUT. Neither test in the diff covers the array form.
issues.fix_hint: Whichever direction the primary question is resolved, add a test pinning the scalar and single-element-array forms to the SAME expansion, and a second pinning `["@kw", "http://ex/ok"]`. If the drop semantics are kept, the array branch must collapse a now-empty result to `None` so the property is dropped rather than materialised as `[]` — but note that collapsing unconditionally would break the genuinely-empty-input cases at src/expand.rs:382-388, so the two must be distinguished.
issues.title: New scalar-vs-array asymmetry: "p": "@kw" yields [] but "p": ["@kw"] yields an empty-array property

issues.body:
`ActiveContext::expand_iri` returns `None` for TWO distinct reasons (crates/sparq-jsonld/src/context/iri.rs:63-85, and its own doc comment says so): a keyword-shaped non-keyword (step 2, iri.rs:68-70) and, under `vocab: true`, a defined term whose IRI mapping is null — an explicit `@id: null` / `"term": null` (step 5, iri.rs:81-85).

Both new/updated tests exercise only the keyword-shaped cause (`"@notakeyword"`, `"@kw"`), and both the code comment and the test names speak only of that case. But the `@type: @vocab` branch at src/expand.rs:893-896 uses `vocab: true`, so the nulled-term cause is silently swept in.

Verified at PR head:
  {"@context": {"@vocab":"http://ex/", "nt": null, "k": {"@type":"@vocab"}}, "k": "nt"} -> []
Previously this produced `[{"http://ex/k": [{"@id": null}]}]`, matching jsonld.js. So a documented behaviour change on an untested path ships under tests that describe only the keyword-shaped path. Whatever the resolution of the primary question, this second cause needs its own pinned case — it is the one users are most likely to hit, since nulling a term in a context is ordinary authoring, whereas a keyword-shaped token is pathological.
issues.fix_hint: Add explicit unit cases for the nulled-term cause under both `@type: @id` and `@type: @vocab` coercion, and state in the `expand_value` doc comment which of the two `expand_iri` -> None causes the chosen semantics applies to, cross-referencing context/iri.rs:63-85.
issues.title: The second cause of a null IRI expansion (a term bound to null) changes behaviour with no test coverage

issues.body:
Two smaller losses in the same hunk:

1. The replacement comment at src/expand.rs:884-887 justifies the behaviour as "A null IRI expansion drops the value rather than manufacturing an empty node reference for callers to retain" — an implementation-convenience statement. The comment it replaces cited §5.3.2 step 1 verbatim, the expand/0122 precedent, and the reference processors. Under this repo's convention (see the `[SONNET-4.6] sq-oy1f.45` / `W3C expand/0122` annotations at src/expand.rs:456-460 and the `W3C expand/pi05` / `pi07, pi09` annotations at src/expand.rs:804-821), a spec-behaviour decision should carry its citation, and a REVERSAL of one especially so.

2. The deleted test dropped the negative assertion `must never produce an empty-string @id`, which pinned the original `unwrap_or_default()` bug. The new `Option` signature does make an empty-string `@id` unreachable through this function, so the guard is not strictly load-bearing — but the history of that specific bug (and the follow-up review noted in the deleted comment) is now recorded nowhere, so a future refactor back to a non-Option return has no tripwire.
issues.fix_hint: Restore a citation to whatever normative text or W3C test supports the final semantics, and either keep an equivalent regression assertion or record the `unwrap_or_default()` / empty-string-@id history in the doc comment so the constraint survives the next refactor.
issues.title: Rewritten comment drops the normative justification, and the empty-string @id regression guard is silently removed

verdict.summary:
The PR changes Value Expansion (JSON-LD 1.1 API §5.3.2 steps 1-2) from the spec-literal `{"@id": <result of IRI expanding value>}` to dropping the value entirely when IRI Expansion returns null, and rewrites the tests to assert the new behaviour. Two blockers.

(1) §5.3.2 steps 1-2 return the single-entry `@id` map UNCONDITIONALLY; only the value may be null. jsonld.js `_expandValue` likewise returns `{'@id': null}`. The diff deletes the prior, explicitly W3C-citation-backed comment (the expand/0122 `"@id": null` precedent) and replaces it with a caller-convenience rationale, with no counter-citation, no W3C test reference, and no conformance evidence (the pinned suite is absent here, so the expand lane SKIPs). The sibling `@id`-KEYWORD path at src/expand.rs:461-464 is left untouched and still stores `{"@id": null}` citing expand/0122, so the crate is now internally inconsistent about the same IRI-Expansion-returns-null condition.

(2) Guarding the property-index prepend on `reexpanded.is_some()` suppresses the spec-MANDATED `invalid value object` abort of step 13.8.3.7.5, and the new test `property_index_null_re_expansion_is_dropped` enshrines the suppression as intended.

Verified empirically against the crate at PR head (out-of-tree probe, no repo files touched):
  `{"@id":"@kw","p":"v"}`                      -> {"@id": null, "http://ex/p": [...]}  (kept)
  `@type:@id` + "@kw"                          -> []                                 (dropped)
  index `{"@kw":"kept"}` on a value object      -> OK
  index `{"real":"kept"}` on a value object     -> ERR InvalidValueObject
  `"p": "@kw"`                                 -> []
  `"p": ["@kw"]`                               -> [{"http://ex/p": []}]

The last pair is a new scalar-vs-array asymmetry, and a term explicitly bound to `null` (the second reason `expand_iri` yields `None`) silently changes behaviour with zero test coverage. Tests are non-vacuous but pin the divergent behaviour.
